rules.title: No-Fault Eviction Relocation Assistance Under the RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting a tenant for an enumerated not-at-fault reason (owner/family/manager occupancy, demolition/conversion/removal from rental use, government order to vacate, HUD-ordered vacation, residential hotel conversion, conversion to affordable housing, or demolition/conversion to condos/hotels/commercial use) from a unit covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) must pay relocation assistance per unit and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving the termination notice, with a copy of the notice filed with LAHD within 3 days of service. Relocation amounts (effective 7/1/2026-6/30/2027) range from $11,000 (eligible tenant, <3 years) to $27,400 (qualified tenant, 3+ years or low income), paid within 15 days of the notice, and increase every July 1.
rules.key_value: $11,000-$27,400 per unit by tenant/tenancy category (Chart A, 7/1/2026-6/30/2027), increasing every July 1; payment due within 15 days of notice

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to rental units covered by the RSO or JCO. Reduced 'Mom and Pop' relocation amounts apply where the building has 4 or fewer rental units, the landlord has not used the provision in the prior 3 years, the landlord owns no more than 4 residential units plus a single-family home on a separate lot in L.A., and only for owner/family-occupancy evictions. Single-family dwellings owned by a natural person (directly or via trust/controlled entity) who owns no more than 4 dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot owe only one month's rent.

rules.exemptions: No relocation assistance owed when: a resident manager is evicted to be replaced by another resident manager (unless the outgoing manager is a Manager-Tenant receiving reduced/free rent, who may still be entitled); eviction is required due to hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by landlord negligence. A landlord may offset a tenant's accumulated unpaid rent against relocation assistance owed, except where the termination is required by a government order to vacate or comply with an unpermitted-dwelling order.
rules.interaction: The Just Cause Ordinance (LAMC 165.03/165.06) applies parallel not-at-fault eviction and relocation rules to non-RSO-covered units; RSO unit withdrawals for demolition/conversion are treated as Ellis Act evictions (Cal. Gov't Code § 7060.4) under LAMC 151.22-151.28.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).
rules.conflict_note: Document gives only the current fee-schedule period (7/1/2026-6/30/2027), not the original enactment/effective date of the underlying RSO/JCO relocation requirement.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) – Demolition for New Construction Relocation & Occupant Protections
rules.requirement: For 'Protected Units' demolished for new construction, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw with LAHD, serve tenants written notice, and provide occupant protections including the right to relocation, the right to remain in the unit up to 6 months before construction begins (with 6-month move-out notice), the right to return to the unit if demolition does not proceed, a right of first refusal to the new building for some tenants, and tenant notification requirements. Lower-income households must be paid enhanced relocation (Chart B); above-low-income households receive RSO/JCO Chart A amounts. The owner must choose one of three compliance options (standardized payment, comparable replacement unit, or individualized relocation) and pay the highest amount required by State and City law.
rules.key_value: Chart B lower-income relocation (7/1/2026-6/30/2027): Extremely Low $115,480; Very Low $96,750; Low Income per Chart A ($14,400 eligible/$27,400 qualified); above-low-income per Chart A ($11,000-$27,400); penalty starting at $250,000 per displaced unit for noncompliance

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies only to 'Protected Units' being demolished for the purpose of new construction, where demolition/withdrawal filing occurs within 5 years of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict. Protected Units include: units subject (now or within the past 5 years) to a rent-restriction covenant/ordinance/law for lower/very-low income persons; units subject to any form of rent or price control (including all RSO units) within the past 5 years; units rented by lower/very-low income households within the past 5 years; or units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.

rules.exemptions: The regular RSO or JCO relocation rules (not the RPO's enhanced rules) apply if the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower-income tenant.
rules.interaction: The RPO codifies and expands the State's Housing Crisis Act (HCA, Cal. Gov't Code § 66300 et seq., originally enacted via SB 330 and later updated by SB 8 and AB 1218); the landlord must pay the higher of the RSO/JCO (Chart A) or RPO (Chart B) amount, and RSO/JCO amounts must also be enhanced for lower-income tenants under the HCA regardless of RPO applicability.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.quoted_span:
On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO which codified and expanded upon 
replacement requirements and occupant protections of the HCA, and enhanced requirements for 
Restricted Affordable Units.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act – Relocation Assistance for Demolition of Protected Units for New Construction
rules.requirement: Under the State's Housing Crisis Act, only lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced for demolition of a unit that the owner will replace with new construction must receive relocation payments consistent with the relocation benefits required to be paid by public entities under Government Code Chapter 16 (commencing with Section 7260); other displaced tenants need only receive the local RSO/JCO minimum amounts, enhanced only if the HCA or RPO requires it.
rules.key_value: Relocation payment per public-entity relocation benefit standards (Gov. Code Ch. 16, § 7260 et seq.) for lower-income (≤80% AMI) households displaced by demolition for new construction

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to lower-income (80% AMI or below) households displaced by demolition of a unit being replaced with new construction.

rules.exemptions: Above-low-income households are not entitled to the enhanced public-entity-level benefit; they receive the local RSO/JCO minimum relocation amounts instead.
rules.interaction: Locally implemented and enhanced in Los Angeles through the Resident Protections Ordinance (L.A. Ord. No. 188481/188482); originally introduced as the Housing Crisis Act of 2019 via SB 330, later updated by SB 8 and AB 1218.
rules.quoted_span:
The City’s Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) and the State’s Housing Crisis Act (HCA) require that ONLY lower income households (80%  AMI or 
lower) being displaced for demolition of their units where the owner will replace the units 
with new construction receive relocation payment consistent to the relocation benefits 
required to be paid by public entities under Chapter 16 (commencing with Section 7260)
rules.conflict_note: Document does not state the original enactment/effective date of Gov. Code § 66300.6 itself, only that the HCA originated via SB 330 (2019) and was later amended by SB 8 and AB 1218.
